name: QuizForge evaluation set v1
note: 20 passage-based and 20 closed-book questions with a single correct answer each; the correct letter is shuffled with a fixed seed.

items.context: Deductive reasoning starts from a general rule and applies it to a particular case. Inductive reasoning observes many specific cases and proposes a general rule.
items.question: Which type of reasoning starts from a general rule and applies it to a particular case?
Which activation function outputs values strictly between 0 and 1?

items.context: Abductive reasoning looks at an observation and infers the most plausible explanation for it. For example, the road is wet, so it probably rained.
items.question: 'The road is wet, so it probably rained' is an example of which type of reasoning?
What is the time complexity of binary search on a sorted array of n elements?

items.context: A laptop costs 60,000 rupees. A 10% discount is given first, and then GST of 18% is charged on the discounted price.
items.question: What is the final price of the laptop?
Which data structure follows the Last-In-First-Out principle?

items.context: BFS explores a graph level by level, guarantees the shortest path in an unweighted graph, and uses a lot of memory. DFS explores one path deeply and uses little memory.
items.question: Which algorithm guarantees the shortest path in an unweighted graph?
Which of the following is a supervised learning task?

items.context: DFS explores one path deeply before backtracking. It uses a stack and needs low memory.
items.question: Which data structure does DFS use?
What is the time complexity of building a binary heap from n unsorted elements using the bottom-up method?

items.context: A* evaluates nodes with f(n) = g(n) + h(n), where g(n) is the actual cost from the start to node n and h(n) is the estimated cost from node n to the goal.
items.question: In A*, what does h(n) represent?

options.B: The depth of the search tree
options.C: The estimated cost from n to the goal
options.D: The actual cost from the start to n

items.question: Which of these sorting algorithms has a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n)?

items.context: In the ReAct framework the AI reasons, takes an action, observes the result, reasons again and then answers.
items.question: In ReAct, what happens immediately after the AI takes an action?
Which regularisation technique tends to produce sparse weight vectors (many weights exactly zero)?

items.context: Chain-of-Thought is best for math and logic, Tree-of-Thought is best for planning, and ReAct is best for agentic AI because it uses tools and external knowledge.
items.question: According to the passage, which method is best for math and logic?
Which mechanism is the core of the Transformer architecture?

items.context: Tree-of-Thought explores multiple reasoning paths. Compared with Chain-of-Thought it is slower, but it gives higher creativity and better decision quality.
items.question: Which method is slower but gives better decision quality?
According to Bayes' theorem, P(A given B) equals which expression?

options.A: P(A given B) x P(B) / P(A)
options.B: P(A) x P(B) / P(B given A)
options.D: P(B given A) x P(A) / P(B)

items.context: STRIPS (Stanford Research Institute Problem Solver) is a classical planning formalism in which each action is defined by its preconditions and its effects.
items.question: What does STRIPS stand for?

options.B: Simple Task Routing and Path Search
options.C: Structured Tree Reasoning In Problem Solving

items.question: In gradient descent, in which direction are the parameters updated?

options.A: Along the gradient of the loss
options.B: Opposite to the gradient of the loss

items.context: The planning cycle is: Goal, Break Tasks, Prioritize, Assign Resources, Execute, Monitor, Replan.
items.question: In the planning cycle, which step comes immediately after Prioritize?
Which metric is the harmonic mean of precision and recall?

items.context: The main sources of uncertainty are missing data, sensor errors, the user changing their mind, and changes in the environment.
items.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a source of uncertainty?
Which layer in a CNN is typically used to reduce the spatial size of feature maps?

items.context: When the environment changes, the AI updates its plan instead of continuing with an outdated one. A delivery robot whose route is blocked finds an alternate route and continues the delivery.
items.question: What is the robot's behaviour called?
Which SQL clause filters individual rows before they are grouped?

items.context: Goal decomposition makes planning easier, allows better resource allocation, leads to faster execution and makes monitoring easier.
items.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of goal decomposition?

options.C: It guarantees that no task ever fails

items.question: What is the decimal number 10 in binary?

items.context: Chain-of-Thought reasoning is slow, needs more computation, and may still reason incorrectly. It is, however, transparent and easy to debug.
items.question: Which is a limitation of Chain-of-Thought?

options.B: It cannot be used for maths

items.question: What is the derivative of x^3 with respect to x?

items.context: Examples of autonomous AI include AI customer support, GitHub Copilot, AI coding agents, healthcare diagnosis, banking chatbots and AI research assistants.
items.question: Which of the following is NOT given as an example of autonomous AI?
What is the capital city of Australia?

items.context: Analogical reasoning solves a new problem by recalling a similar past situation and adapting its solution. It is the basis of case-based recommendation.
items.question: Case-based recommendation is based on which type of reasoning?
Which is the largest planet in the Solar System?

items.context: DFS explores one path deeply before backtracking. It uses a stack and needs low memory. It does not guarantee the shortest path.
items.question: Which statement about DFS is true?
What is the chemical symbol for sodium?

items.context: ReAct is the only one of the three methods that routinely uses tools and external knowledge, which is why it is the most agent-like.
items.question: Which method routinely uses tools and external knowledge?
What is 15 percent of 200?

items.context: BFS explores level by level and guarantees the shortest path in an unweighted graph. Its disadvantage is high memory usage, because the whole frontier must be stored.
items.question: What is a drawback of BFS?

options.B: It cannot find the shortest path

items.question: A perfectly balanced binary search tree holds 1,023 nodes. How many levels (height in levels) does it have?
